titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Altar and the Ark (ch. 103)
part: ch. 103 — The Altar and the Ark
about: The Ark is explained as the altar of the church: the table is the tomb, the prosphora the body of Christ, the stone the sealed grave. The chapter then turns on the Jews and idolaters, citing Isaiah 44 and Psalm 96.

sentences.i: Chapter 103: Concerning the Horns of the Altar
sentences.n: Chapter heading. አቅርንተ is the construct plural of ቀርን 'horn' (አቅርንት), so 'horns-of altar'; በእንተ 'concerning' takes the construct. The numeral ፻፫ is 100 + 3.

sentences.t: ታቦትሰ ፡ አቅርንተ ፡ ምሥዋዕ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ይሠውዑ ፡ ቅዱሳን ፡ ካህናት ፡ ወዘያነብሩ ፡ ዲቤሁ ፡ ጠረጲዛ ፡ አምሳለ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ተቀብረ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ጎልጎታ ፡ መቃብር ፤
sentences.l: The-ark indeed (is) horns-of altar, it, where sacrifice holy priests, and-which they-set upon-it table, likeness-of where was-buried in-midst-of Golgotha tomb;
sentences.i: As for the Ark, it is the horns of the altar, where the holy priests offer sacrifice; and on it they set a table, a likeness of the place where He was buried, in the midst of Golgotha, the tomb;
sentences.n: ታቦትሰ: the enclitic -ሰ marks a contrast or topic ('as for the Ark'). ውእቱ 'it is' is the copula. ኀበ 'where' + ይሠውዑ 3mp imperfect 'they sacrifice' (root ሠ-ወ-ዐ). ወዘያነብሩ 'and that which they set' (ወ + ዘ + 3mp imperfect of the causative አነበረ). አምሳለ is a construct ('likeness of') governing the clause ኀበ ተቀብረ, a pattern for reading the church altar as a copy of a sacred place. ተቀብረ is the passive/reflexive (Gt) 'was buried'. Here the Ark is the altar-slab, and the table above it the tomb, an interpretation built on Gospel burial imagery.

sentences.t: ወዘመልዕልተ ፡ ጠረጲዛ ፡ ጵርስፎራ ፡ አምሳለ ፡ አጵርጌ ፡ ዘውእቱ ፡ ሥጋሁ ፡ ለአማኑኤል ፡ አክራጦስ ፡ ንጹሕ ፡ ዘአልቦቱ ፡ ቱስሕተ ፡ እንተ ፡ ነሥአ ፡ መድኀኒነ ፡ እማርያም ፤
sentences.l: and-that-which above table prosphora, likeness-of apurge(?), which it (is) body-his of-Emmanuel, akratos, pure, who not-to-him ṭusḥət(?), which took our-saviour from-Mary;
sentences.i: and what is above the table is the prosphora, a likeness of the apurge (?), which is the body of Emmanuel, unmixed (?) and pure, without fault (?), which our Saviour took from Mary;
sentences.n: ጵርስፎራ is the Greek prosphora, the offered bread of the Eucharist. አጵርጌ is obscure to me; I leave it as 'apurge (?)', not guessing a meaning. አማኑኤል is Emmanuel (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:23). አክራጦስ is Greek akratos, 'unmixed, pure' (?), as the glossary already hedges. ዘአልቦቱ 'who has not' (ዘ + አልቦ + -ቱ); ቱስሕተ I take as 'fault, error' (?), related to ስሕተት, but the form is unusual and Dillmann is not at hand. እንተ is the feminine relative, agreeing with ሥጋ; ነሥአ 'took' (n-ś-ʾ); እማርያም 'from Mary' (እም-).

sentences.t: ዘይቤሎሙ ፡ ለሐዋርያቲሁ ፡ ቅዱሳን ፡ ብልዑ ፡ ሥጋየ ፡ ወዘሰ ፡ ኢበልዐ ፡ ሥጋየ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ክፍለ ፡ ምስሌየ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ሕይወተ ፡ ዘለዓለም ፡ ወዘሰ ፡ በልዐ ፡ ሥጋየ ፡ እመኒ ፡ ሞተ ፡ የሐዩ ፡ ለዓለም ፡ ወተሳተፈ ፡ ሥጋየ ፡ ወደምየ ፡ ወኮነ ፡ መዋርስትየ ፡ ወይብሎ ፡ ለአቡየ ፡ አንተ ፡ አቡነ ፡ ዘበሰማያት ፤
sentences.l: who said-to-them to-his-apostles holy: 'Eat my-flesh; and-whoever not-ate my-flesh, there-is-not share with-me and-there-is-not life of-eternity; but-whoever ate my-flesh, even-if he-died, he-will-live for-ever, and-he-partook-of my-flesh and-my-blood and-became my-heir, and-he-says to-my-father, You (are) our-father who (is) in-heavens;
sentences.i: who said to His holy apostles: 'Eat my flesh. And whoever does not eat my flesh has no share with me and no eternal life; but whoever eats my flesh, even if he dies, will live for ever, and has shared in my flesh and my blood and become my heir, and says to my Father, You are our Father who is in the heavens;
sentences.n: This is a free paraphrase of John 6:53-58, with the Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:9) at the end. ዘይቤሎሙ 'who said to them' (ዘ + ይቤ + -ሎሙ). ብልዑ is the 2mp imperative of በልዐ 'eat'. ወዘሰ 'and whoever' (ወ + ዘ + -ሰ). ኢበልዐ negated perfect; አልቦ 'there is not' is the negative existential. ክፍለ and ሕይወተ are accusatives after አልቦ. እመኒ ሞተ የሐዩ: 'even if he died he will live' (perfect in the if-clause, imperfect in the result). ወተሳተፈ is a Gt perfect 'shared in'. ወይብሎ ... አንተ አቡነ: the believer addresses God; the speaker's 'my father' becomes 'our father' in the quoted prayer. The verbs shift from perfect to imperfect freely in this sentence.

sentences.t: ወአብኒ ፡ ይሰጠዎ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብሎ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ አንተ ።
sentences.l: and-the-Father also, he-gives-to-him, while he-says-to-him, My-son (are) you.
sentences.i: And the Father also answers him, saying to him, 'You are my son.'
sentences.n: ወአብኒ: አብ 'father' with -ኒ 'also'. ይሰጠዎ is read here as 'he answers/replies to him' (?) from ሰጠወ; I am uncertain of the exact verb, and the sense 'gives to him' is possible, so it is hedged (?). እንዘ ይብሎ 'while he says to him' (conjunction + imperfect). ወልድየ አንተ 'my son (are) you' (vocative-like noun + pronoun). The Father's reply echoes Psalm 2:7 and the baptism voice.

sentences.t: ወአክሊል ፡ እንተ ፡ መልዕልተ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ጵርስፎራ ፡ አምሳለ ፡ እብን ፡ እንተ ፡ ኀተምዋ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ መቃብር ፨
sentences.l: And-crown which above it (is) prosphora, likeness-of stone which they-sealed-it Jews upon tomb.
sentences.i: And the crown that is above it is the prosphora, a likeness of the stone that the Jews sealed upon the tomb.
sentences.n: አክሊል 'crown' here names the covering piece on the altar. እንተ መልዕልተ 'which (is) above' (feminine relative + preposition). ኀተምዋ 'they sealed it' (3mp perfect + -ዋ 'her/it'); the stone is feminine in Geʿez (እብን), hence the feminine relative እንተ. The allusion is to the stone and seal on the tomb (Matthew 27:66). The sign ፨ closes the unit.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ይብል ፡ ካህን ፡ ፈኑ ፡ መንፈሰ ፡ ቅዱሰ ፡ ይትፌነው ፡ መንፈስ ፡ ቅዱስ ፡ ወይከውን ፡ ሥጋሁ ፡ ለእግዚእነ ፡ ፍጹመ ፡ ወሶበ ፡ ተመጠውነ ፡ ንከውን ፡ ሱቱፋነ ፡ ለሥጋ ፡ ወደም ፡ ለእግዚእነ ፡ ወመድኀኒነ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ወልደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ሕያው ፡ ወመንፈስ ፡ ቅዱስ ፡ እ ፡ ምይእዜ ፡ ወእስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፨
sentences.l: And-when says priest, 'Send spirit holy, let-be-sent Spirit Holy, and-let-be body-his of-our-Lord perfect' and-when we-partake, we-shall-be sharers of-flesh and-blood of-our-Lord and-our-saviour Jesus Christ, son-of God living, and-Spirit Holy, from now and-until for-ever.
sentences.i: And when the priest says, 'Send the Holy Spirit; may the Holy Spirit be sent, and may the body of our Lord be made perfect' — and when we receive communion, we become sharers in the flesh and blood of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, and of the Holy Spirit, from now and for ever.
sentences.n: This is the invocation of the Spirit (epiclesis) in the liturgy. ፈኑ is the 2ms imperative of ፈነወ 'send'. ይትፌነው is a Gt jussive, 'let him be sent / let him come' (the shape is odd, so the reading is a little uncertain (?)). መንፈሰ ቅዱሰ: the construct-looking ending is Bezold's form, an accusative after the imperative. ተመጠውነ 'we were given / we partook' (Gt of መጠወ, 'receive the gift', used for communion); ንከውን 'we shall be'. ሱቱፋነ 'sharers' is a predicate accusative plural. ወልደ እግዚኣብሔር ሕያው: 'son of God the living' (Matthew 16:16). The final phrase እ ፡ ምይእዜ is printed with a separate እ, presumably እም 'from' (?); ምይእዜ 'now'.

sentences.t: ወንግሩኬ ፡ ለለ ፡ ፩፩ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይትመክሑ ፡ ላዕሌነ ፡ ዕዉራነ ፡ ልብ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ ፀርነ ፡ ወፀረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላክነ ፤
sentences.l: And-tell then to-each one(?), that not they-boast over-us, blind-ones-of heart, Jews, our-enemy and-enemy-of God our-God;
sentences.i: And so tell each one, that they may not boast over us — the Jews, blind of heart, our enemy and the enemy of God our God;
sentences.n: ወንግሩኬ is the 2mp imperative of ነገረ 'tell' with ወ- 'and' and the particle -ኬ 'then, so'. ለለ ፩፩ is 'to each one' (ለለ 'each, every' with the numeral 1 written twice, ፩፩, read as 'one by one' (?)). ከመ ኢይትመክሑ is 'that they not boast' (ከመ ኢ- + Gt jussive of መክሐ). ዕዉራነ ልብ is a construct, 'blind ones of heart'; አይሁድ stands in apposition. ፀርነ 'our enemy' and ፀረ 'enemy of' (construct) are the same noun ፀር.

sentences.t: ወይብሉ ፡ ብዙኅ ፡ አማልክቲሆሙ ፡ ወይሰግዲ ፡ ለዕፀው ፡ ወይብሉ ፡ ተዘሚሮሙ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ነገረ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ለመንፈቁ ፡ ትሰግዲ ፡ ወበመንፈቁ ፡ ትጠብሱ ፡ ሥጋ ፡ ወትበልዑ ፤
sentences.l: and-they-say 'many (are) their-gods', and-they-bow to-trees, and-they-say, singing(?), where word-of Isaiah prophet: 'for-its-half you-bow, and-with-its-half you-roast flesh and-you-eat';
sentences.i: and they say, 'Their gods are many,' and they bow down to trees. And they say, chanting (?), as in the word of the prophet Isaiah: 'With half of it you bow down, and with half of it you roast flesh and eat';
sentences.n: ተዘሚሮሙ is a Gt participial form of ዘመረ 'sing' and means 'singing/chanting' (?), though the sense here may be 'making a mock-song'; I hedge it. ኀበ ነገረ 'where (is) the word of' (ነገረ is a construct). The quotation is a loose citation of Isaiah 44:15-17 (a man burns half the wood and bows to the rest). The verbs ትሰግዲ, ትጠብሱ, ትበልዑ are 2mp imperfects, and ሰገደ 'bow down' takes ለ- for its object. ለመንፈቁ 'for its half' (መንፈቅ 'half' + -ሁ), በመንፈቁ 'with its half'.

sentences.t: ይብል ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ በእንተ ፡ እለ ፡ ይሰግዲ ፡ ለግልፎ ፡ ወለጣዖት ፤
sentences.l: says Isaiah thus concerning those-who bow to-carved-image and-to-idol;
sentences.i: Isaiah speaks thus about those who bow down to the carved image and to the idol;
sentences.n: ይብል 'says' (defective ብህለ). በእንተ እለ 'concerning those who' (እለ is the plural relative). ግልፎ 'carved image' and ጣዖት 'idol' (loan word) are both marked with ለ-, the object marker after ሰገደ. The allusion is to Isaiah 44:9-20, the passage against idol-makers.

sentences.t: ወይብሉ ፡ እሉ ፡ አማልክቲነ ፡ ወፈጠሩነ ፡ ይብልዎሙ ፡ ወይሰግዲ ፡ ሎሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላኮሙ ፤
sentences.l: and-they-say, 'These (are) our-gods and-created-us', they-say-to-them, and-they-bow to-them as God their-God;
sentences.i: And they say, 'These are our gods, and they created us (?)'; they speak to them and bow down to them as to God their God;
sentences.n: ወፈጠሩነ 'and they created us' (ፈጠረ 'create', with -ነ 'us'); in the Isaiah source the idol-maker asks it to deliver him (Isaiah 44:17), so the sense may be 'saved us' or 'made us' (?). ይብልዎሙ 'they say to them' (3mp + -ዎሙ); the pronoun ሎሙ 'to them' follows ይሰግዲ. ከመ እግዚኣብሔር አምላኮሙ 'as (to) God, their god' is the comparison. The quotation is bound loosely to the next verses.

sentences.t: እሉኬ ፡ እለ ፡ ያስሕትዎሙ ፡ አጋንንት ፡ በእከዮሙ ፡ ወዳዊትኒ ፡ ይቤ ፡ በእንቲአሆሙ ፡ አማልክቲሆሙ ፡ ለአሕዛብ ፡ አጋንንት ፡ ወእግዚኣብሔርሰ ፡ ሰማያተ ፡ ገብረ ፡ አሚን ፡ ወሠናይት ፡ ቅድሜሁ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: These-then (are) those-who cause-to-err-them demons, by-their-evil; and-David also said concerning-them, 'Their-gods of-the-nations (are) demons; and-God indeed made the-heavens; faith(?) and-beauty (are) before-him.'
sentences.i: These, then, are the ones whom demons lead astray by their evil. And David also spoke about them: 'The gods of the nations are demons; but God made the heavens. Faith (?) and goodness are before Him.'
sentences.n: ያስሕትዎሙ is the causative (አስሕተ) 3mp imperfect with -ዎሙ 'them', 'they lead them astray'; the subject አጋንንት 'demons' follows. በእከዮሙ 'by their evil'. The quotation is Psalm 96:5-6 (95:5-6 in the Greek numbering): 'the gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens'. ወእግዚኣብሔርሰ: the enclitic -ሰ marks the contrast. አሚን in the psalm line is probably 'faith/trust' (?), but it could be 'truly'; ወሠናይት 'goodness, beauty' (?) is the psalm's 'splendour'. ቅድሜሁ 'before him'. The closing ፨ ፨ ፨ ends the chapter.
